newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila likely to buy wheat, rice, to boost stocks.
newsitem.headline: Manila likely to buy wheat, rice, to boost stocks.

text.p: Philippine grain importers will probably be in the market to buy more rice and wheat next week as the country seeks to bolster its food buffer stocks, traders said on Friday.
"Rice and wheat will still be the play next week," a senior trader at one of the country's largest flour millers said.
Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero told reporters on Friday the state-owned National Food Authority is considering buying rice from two private groups in Pakistan.
Escudero told reporters the NFA had to expedite all rice orders so the country's buffer stocks could be replenished before the seasonally lean third quarter of this year.
The Philippine summer which arrives in the second quarter of the year normally curtails rice production since most of the farms in the country are not irrigated.
The NFA has been authorised by President Ramos to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice to head off any inflationary supply crunch for the staple food of the Philippines' 70 million people.
Another executive at a flour mill in Manila also said his company will be wathing the market closely next week.
"We will buy if the price is right for our April requirements," he said.
The Philippines buys most of its wheat in Minneapolis, where the MGE's March wheat contract closed on Thursday 5-1/4 U.S. cents higher at $4.05-3/4 a bushel.
Traders said Philippine wheat buyers are also going back to U.S. suppliers due to delays in shipments of previous orders from Canada.
The NFA recently clinched deals to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice each from Vietnam and China and some 205,000 tonnes from Thailand.
In the wheat market, Philippine flour millers are expected to buy wheat on dips in U.S. prices to secure their March and April requirements.
One Philippine mill sought tenders for 25,000 tonnes of spring wheat and 15,000 tonnes of white wheat, but rejected the bids on Wednesday because of high prices.
"We will look at the market again next week," an executive in the firm said.
Philippine firms have asked suppliers of Canadian wheat to trim their prices on orders for delivery this month due to the backlog, flour mill officials and traders said.

"Our supplier of Canadian spring wheat told us he could not meet the agreed delivery date due to weather problems. We agreed for a later delivery as long as there is just compensation, such as a price reduction," one executive said.
He said the Philippines bought about 25,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat for delivery in February and early March.
Grains traders said rumours were circulating in the market that between 60,000-100,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat bought by Philippine firms for prompt shipment have been delayed.
Domestic flour prices remained steady at 290 pesos per 25-kg bag of hard flour and 260 pesos per 25-kg bag for soft flour, a survey by the Philippine Trade and Industry Department showed.
The local corn market is expected to be quiet next week as livestock farmers and feed millers wait for the arrival of 117,000 tonnes of yellow corn imported from China.
"The Chinese corn is expected to arrive in early March," said one trader.
The NFA said the average retail price of yellow corn rose to 10.62 pesos a kg from 10.59 pesos while the price for a kg of white corn fell to 10.91 pesos a kg from 10.96.
Farmgate prices of yellow corn also inched up to 6.83 pesos a kg from 6.82 pesos while the price of white corn increased to 6.94 pesos per kg from 6.90.
US$1 = P26.30 pesos
